summary: Shard-routing header mismatch in proxy leads to suppressed rerank scores and intermittent latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that for short queries (<=6 tokens) their reranker returns very low similarity scores or no candidates, and they are seeing intermittent 503s and 200+ ms tail latency on the rerank endpoint. Behavior started after a proxy rollout on 2026-03-09 that added multiplexed shard headers for embedding requests.

Impact:
- Affects AcmeCommerce Dedicated cluster in us-west-2.
- Query quality regression: relevant documents dropped from results for short queries.
- Intermittent latency spikes and 5xx responses for rerank calls.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity, prod-us-west-2
- Proxy version: proxy-service v2.9.1 deployed 2026-03-09
- Serving runtime: rw-serving-1.6.
- Customer pins model rw-rerank-base-v1 and uses rw-embed-small-v3 for embeddings.

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Send embed request for short query: "price" (1 token) with header X-Embed-Shard: shard-b
2) Immediately call /rerank with embedding payload and model=rw-rerank-base-v1
3) Observe rerank returns empty top-10 or very low scores (0.02-0.05) and occasional 503 status codes.

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer provided request/response traces (attached).
- Proxy access logs show fanout to two shard backends; one backend returns 404 for embedding lookup in ~12% of requests.
- Serving runtime logs show KV-cache misses and short-query path routed to CPU fallback when shard header mismatches are present.

Hypothesis:
The new multiplexing header causes a shard routing mismatch for short-length embeddings. The reranker expects a canonical embedding id namespace per customer; the proxy sometimes rewrites or omits the embedding namespace header resulting in a silent fallback to a different shard or CPU path. Short queries produce embeddings that are compact and more sensitive to shard boundaries, leading to suppressed similarity scores when compared across mis-routed shards. Additionally, the proxy's synchronous fanout to multiple shard replicas increases tail latency when one replica is overloaded after the rollout.
comments: Support (Aisha Kapoor) 2026-03-10: Opened ticket after customer supplied traces and repro steps. Customer says issue began immediately after proxy update on 2026-03-09. Requested request IDs and time window for SRE to investigate.

Customer (Jared Mills, AcmeCommerce) 2026-03-10: Provided request IDs and a short script that reliably reproduces the empty top results for queries shorter than 7 tokens. Noting problem is blocking a live pricing feature; flagged as high impact.

SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-11: Initial triage: reproduced locally against dedicated test cluster using snapshot of customer's routing config. Observed header X-Embed-Shard occasionally stripped by proxy middleware when token count metadata is missing. Reproduced 503s under simulated load due to fanout queueing when one replica returned 404s. Added logs to proxy to capture header propagation.

Eng (Marta Ruiz) 2026-03-11: Confirmed that the proxy introduces a fallback when header validation fails. Proposed short-term mitigation: add a conservative header-preservation patch to proxy and route short queries to canonical shard by default. Creating PR for quick rollback.

Support (Aisha Kapoor) 2026-03-12: Notified customer of temporary mitigation (header-preservation filter) applied to their routing layer. Asked customer to validate behavior and provide updated traces.
Customer (Jared Mills) 2026-03-12: Reports immediate quality improvement for short queries; 503s reduced. Will monitor for 24 hours and confirm SLA status.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - Triage performed on dedicated staging replica; intermittent header drop reproducible when requests come through legacy health-check proxy path.

2026-03-11 11:05 UTC - Traced class of requests: tokenization lower than threshold caused middleware to skip adding X-Token-Count header; proxy validation logic treated missing token-count as invalid and dropped X-Embed-Shard on rewrite.

2026-03-11 13:30 UTC - Observed that mis-routed shard lookups return 404 which triggers the serving runtime to perform CPU fallback scoring resulting in much lower similarity values for compact embeddings.
2026-03-11 15:00 UTC - Load test showed that proxy fanout to N replicas amplifies tail latency when any replica returns errors. Identified replica grief window of ~250ms added to P95 latency.
2026-03-11 18:40 UTC - Created PR to add header-preservation filter and default-canonical-shard mapping for queries with token_count <=6. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/3712
resolution: 2026-03-12 - Applied hotfix to customer's routing: header-preservation middleware enabled and default canonical shard mapping for short queries. This prevents shard header being stripped and routes short queries to canonical shard-b.
Mitigation effect: Customer reports rerank score distribution returned to expected range for short queries and 503s reduced by ~90% in observed window. Latency P95 improved by ~180ms.

Longer-term fix: Proxy team to harden header validation logic to avoid dropping X-Embed-Shard when token_count header is missing. Also scheduled: better integration tests that include short-query paths, and a config flag to disable synchronous fanout in dedicated clusters during shard degradation windows. Assigned engineering story: INT-4421.

Follow-up actions: monitor customer-specific telemetry for 72 hours; run canary across other dedicated clusters to ensure no regressions; update runbook at https://confluence.redwood/cases/2026/embedding-proxy-shard-runbook.
